title: Press During And After The First World War
definition: A period of intense state-sponsored censorship and repressive legislation (1914-1920) followed by a transition toward nationalist mobilization through the press, marking the shift from colonial control to the Gandhian era of journalism.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the evolution of Indian nationalism, the colonial state's 'security' apparatus, and the role of media in mass mobilization during the Home Rule and Non-Cooperation movements.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Press During And After The First World War.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
